transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brought me in is that things just got really out of hand for me recently. I do landscaping, and usually, I'm just a normal crew guy. But a little while ago, I just... I went into overdrive. I started trying to run three different bids all at once, calling city people, lining up all these plant suppliers... I was messaging everybody I knew about this big park idea I had. It was like I just couldn’t shut it off, and I realized I needed to come talk to someone about it.
In the days or weeks leading up to this burst of energy and activity, had you been using any alcohol, drugs, caffeine, or other substances more than usual?
No, not really. I mean, I drink coffee in the mornings like I always do, but I wasn't drinking more of it than usual. And I don't really drink alcohol or do any drugs. So, no, nothing like that.
How long did this period of increased energy and activity last before things started to settle down or change?

I'd say it was about two weeks. That whole... fired-up, overconfident stretch started right when I began trying to remake myself for that big park pitch I was talking about. I just kept going and going for those two weeks straight, and then... yeah, then I just crashed.

Before this recent two-week period, have you ever had another stretch of time—lasting days or weeks—where you felt unusually low, depressed, or lacking energy, or another time where you felt this same kind of high energy and excitement?

Yeah. I haven't really had that high energy thing before, but the low part... yeah. Honestly, the depression has been hanging over me for about a year now. I was just kind of dragging through work and life for months. Then I had that two-week stretch where I was going a hundred miles an hour, but since I came down from that... man, this latest crash is definitely the worst it's gotten. It's just really heavy right now.
During those two weeks of high energy, did you notice you needed much less sleep than usual but still felt rested?

No, I wouldn't say I needed less sleep. I mean, I was still sleeping my usual amount, maybe seven or eight hours a night. I didn't feel like I could just run on two hours of sleep or anything like that. I just had all this energy during the day when I was awake.
During that two-week period of high energy, did you feel unusually self-confident or like you had special abilities or ideas that were far more important than they really were?

Yeah, I really did. I mean, I honestly believed I was about to become the guy every town around here called for sustainable landscaping. I was so sure I had this brilliant new approach that was going to change everything. Looking back... I mean, I'm still just trying to keep my small jobs paid up, you know? But for those two weeks, I felt like I was the most important landscaper in the state.

During that two-week period of high energy and confidence, did it cause any serious problems—like losing clients, missing deadlines, or conflicts with family or coworkers—or did people just notice you seemed different without it really disrupting your work or relationships?

No, it didn't really cause any problems. I didn't lose any clients or get into any fights or anything like that. People definitely noticed I was... you know, talking a lot more and just really hyped up about my plans, but it didn't mess up my work or my relationships. I was just getting a ton done, honestly.
